bib.title: Bias in error estimation when using cross-validation for model selection

question: Is the cross-validation error estimate of a classifier whose parameters were tuned by minimising CV error an unbiased estimate of its true error on independent data?
hypothesis: Tuning parameters by minimising CV error is training done outside the CV loop, so the minimum CV error may be a biased estimate of true error, and nesting the tuning inside an outer CV loop should remove the bias.
contributions: Show by simulation on null data that the minimum CV error of an optimised Shrunken Centroids and SVM classifier is substantially optimistically biased
Show that nested CV gives an almost unbiased estimate for null and non-null data
Explain the bias as parameter selection bias that adds to the inherent resampling bias

method.summary: Simulated Gaussian two-class microarray-like datasets. For Shrunken Centroids (10-fold CV over delta) and a simplified SVM (LOOCV over a C, gamma grid) the parameter minimising CV error was chosen, the CV error at that optimum was compared with the true error on 20000 independent samples, and then with a nested CV estimate in which the whole tuning procedure is repeated in each outer fold.
method.task: error estimation for tuned binary classifiers (model selection vs. performance estimation)

datasets.name: Synthetic null data
datasets.size: at least 1000 datasets per simulation, each 40 samples (20 per class) x 6000 features; test set 20000 samples
datasets.split: 40 training samples per dataset; 20000 independent test samples from the same distribution
datasets.source: simulated; both classes mean-zero unit-variance multivariate Normal

datasets.name: Synthetic non-null data
datasets.size: 40 training samples x 6000 features, 20000 test samples
datasets.source: simulated; 10 of 6000 genes have mean 1 in class 2, rest mean 0, unit variance

models.name: Shrunken Centroids (Tibshirani et al.)
models.architecture: nearest centroid with centroids shrunk toward overall centroid by delta

other.tie rule: larger delta chosen if two have the same CV error

models.name: Gaussian-kernel SVM with t-statistic feature selection (simplified from Peng et al.)
models.architecture: SVM, Gaussian kernel, top 3 features by absolute two-sample t-statistic chosen inside each fold

other.simplification: RFE replaced by t-statistic top 3; genetic algorithm replaced by fixed Gaussian kernel grid search

training.objective: classifier trained on all 40 samples with the CV-optimal parameter (delta* or C*,gamma*)

other.note: classical models; no gradient training details; random seeds not stated

inference.samples: at least 1000 simulated 40-sample datasets per simulation; one 20000-sample test set per dataset for true error

parameters.nested CV inner loop: 10-fold CV for Shrunken Centroids on the 39 remaining samples; LOOCV grid search for SVM
parameters.inner folds for SVM nested: inferred: LOOCV on 39 samples, from 'exactly the same procedure' and Fig 4 title 'nested LOOCV'

metrics.name: CV error estimate
metrics.definition: average error over left-out samples at the parameter minimising CV error

metrics.name: True error
metrics.definition: mean error of the classifier trained on all 40 samples on 20000 independent samples

metrics.name: Bias
metrics.definition: CV error estimate minus true error (Table 1 mean bias is negative when the estimate is optimistic)

metrics.name: Nested CV error estimate
metrics.definition: outer leave-one-out; tuning repeated on the other 39 samples in each fold

baselines: non-nested CV error at the optimum
eval.protocol: Empirical distributions over simulated datasets (Figs 1-4); no significance tests; no confidence intervals or seeds reported.

limits: Only two classifiers, one data generator (Gaussian, 40 samples, 6000 features), two-class problems.
SVM search simplified (fixed Gaussian kernel, 3 t-statistic features) and authors concede this may reduce the bias observed.
Nested CV uses 39 rather than 40 samples inside the loop, giving a small pessimistic bias.
No variance of the nested estimate, no confidence intervals, no seeds, no code released.
Non-null nested CV tested for SVM; the null nested case is shown for Shrunken Centroids only; the nested non-null Shrunken Centroids result is claimed in the abstract without a figure in the text.
Argument that the bias is general across resampling schemes is intuitive (Eq. 8), not tested for other CV schemes or bootstrap.

terms.definition: takes a set of samples and does feature selection and classifier training and returns a single, well defined classifier
additional bias, always negative, from variance of resampled error estimates when a parameter is chosen to minimise them
bias of a resampling estimator even without parameter selection, e.g. over-estimation from training on a subset
two CV loops: the inner loop is part of the wrapper algorithm that tunes parameters, the outer loop computes the estimate of true error
